authors: Vogeler, J.C., Braaten, J.D., Slesak, R.A. & Falkowski, M.J.
title: Extracting the full value of the Landsat archive: Inter-sensor harmonization for the mapping of Minnesota forest canopy cover (1973-2015)
relevance: The closest published analogue to our entire project on the temporal-canopy side: a 42-year CANOPY COVER series built across multiple sensor generations, peer-reviewed, where inter-sensor harmonization is the central problem rather than a footnote. Gives us a worked precedent for what harmonizing a multi-decade canopy archive actually requires, and how the resulting series is validated - which is exactly the gap Search 23 found in the ML literature. Read it before designing our own harmonization; it is 42 years at coarse resolution where we are 24 years at fine, so the sensor problem is harder there and the spatial problem harder here.

authors: Li, W., Sun, K. & Wei, J.
title: Adapting cross-sensor high-resolution remote sensing imagery for land use classification
relevance: Separates the two problems our 2017 matched pair can now isolate: positional encoding to absorb RESOLUTION differences, and random AMPLITUDE MIXUP to absorb SPECTRAL/style inconsistency. That is independent convergence on the amplitude-equals-style thread from FDA (ID 136), and it validates treating GSD and sensor as distinct axes rather than one 'domain'. Its dynamic pseudo-labelling stage carries the usual confirmation-bias risk (ID 89) and should be treated as optional, but the two-axis architecture is the transferable idea.
